Choose the one that fits your situation. 🔍 Use Case 1: Pre-Purchase Inspection You're considering buying a used car. You want to know if the engine is healthy before you commit. Compression test - shows cylinder health Borescope inspection - reveals internal cylinder wear Visual inspection - condition of ancillaries, belts, hoses Wear analysis - can reveal mileage discrepancies Future cost estimate - likely repairs and lifespan Best for: Used car buyers, private sales, auction purchases, classic car buyers ⚠️ Use Case 2: Failure Inspection Your engine has failed or is showing symptoms. You need to understand the extent of the damage before deciding on repair or replacement. Failure mode analysis - identifies what caused the failure Borescope - shows extent of internal damage Oil analysis - detects debris contamination Repair vs replace assessment - determines if repair is possible Cost-effective recommendation - written recommendation Best for: Owners with unexplained failure, warning lights, or unusual noises "The most expensive mistake in used car buying is trusting the seller's word. A £200 inspection can save you £4,500 on a car with a failing engine. The inspection is the best insurance you can buy." - UK Engine Specialist Interview #32 [EM-INTERVIEW] (full names withheld at specialist's request) Get inspection quotes → Get a quote Critical Difference Inspection vs Diagnostics - What's the Difference? They're complementary services - not alternatives. Here's how they compare. Aspect Diagnostics Inspection Primary method OBD2 scan, ECU code reading, live data Physical examination, compression, borescope, oil analysis What it finds Electrical and sensor faults, emission issues Physical wear, internal damage, mechanical condition Tools used Diagnostic scanner, multimeter Compression tester, borescope, oil analysis kit Time required 30-90 minutes 1-4 hours Typical cost £50-£200 £100-£300 Best for Warning lights, sensor faults, drivability issues Pre-purchase, suspected internal damage, high-mileage vehicles When to Use Each Scenario Recommended Service Engine management light on Diagnostics - code reading reveals the issue Buying a used car Inspection - physical health check of the engine Knocking noise from engine Inspection - physical examination to determine internal damage Loss of power / limp mode Diagnostics - code reading reveals sensor or system faults High-mileage car, unknown history Inspection - check for wear and hidden damage Failed MOT on emissions Diagnostics - identify root cause Classic car purchase Inspection - borescope and compression test Suspected head gasket failure Inspection - compression and leak-down test "Diagnostics tell you what the computer thinks is wrong. Inspection tells you what's actually physically wrong. They're complementary - not alternatives. If you have a warning light, start with diagnostics. If you're buying a car, start with inspection." - UK Engine Specialist Interview #33 [EM-INTERVIEW] Inspection Service What Inspection Includes A professional engine inspection covers these critical components. 👁️ Visual Inspection External condition, belts, hoses, leaks, corrosion, ancillaries Identifies visible issues - leaks, worn belts, damaged components 📊 Compression Test Cylinder pressure - all cylinders measured and compared Reveals worn piston rings, damaged valves, head gasket issues 💨 Leak-Down Test How well each cylinder holds pressure - identifies leakage path Pinpoints exact cause of compression loss - valves, rings, head gasket 🔬 Borescope Inspection Internal view of cylinders, piston crowns, cylinder walls Reveals scoring, damage, carbon buildup - hidden wear 🧪 Oil Analysis (optional) Metal content, contamination, viscosity Detects internal wear (metal particles), coolant contamination, fuel dilution 💧 Coolant Condition Colour, contamination, pH level Indicates head gasket failure or cooling system issues ⚙️ Ancillary Condition Alternator, starter, turbo (if accessible), water pump Condition of supporting components - likely future failures ⛓️ Timing Component Check Condition of timing belt/chain, tensioners, guides (if accessible) Prevents catastrophic timing failure 📄 Written Report Findings, pass/fail status, photos, recommendations You get a clear, actionable summary ⚠️ What's NOT Included Item Why It's Excluded OBD2 code reading That's diagnostics - a separate service (available on request) Repairs Inspection identifies issues - repairs are separate Guarantee of future performance Inspection is a snapshot - not a guarantee Parts replacement Inspection identifies issues - parts are separate Proprietary Data Inspection Cost Data Real pricing from supplier quotes and interviews [EM-QUOTE]. What You Get What You Get - The Inspection Report Your inspection report will include the following sections. 📋 Vehicle Details Make, model, year, mileage, engine code 👁️ Visual Inspection Photos and notes on external condition, leaks, belts, hoses, ancillaries 📊 Compression Test Results Figures per cylinder (psi/bar) with pass/fail status 💨 Leak-Down Test Results Percentage leak per cylinder, identified leakage path 🔬 Borescope Images Images of cylinder walls, piston crowns, valves 🧪 Oil Analysis (if selected) Metal content, contamination, viscosity results 📊 Overall Condition Assessment Pass, advisory, or fail status 💰 Future Cost Estimate Estimated repair or replacement costs ✅ Recommendation Repair, replace, or walk away (for pre-purchase) What "Pass," "Advisory," and "Fail" Mean ✅ Pass Engine is in good condition - no significant issues Proceed with purchase / continue driving ⚠️ Advisory Minor issues found - some wear, minor leaks Budget for future repairs - proceed with caution ❌ Fail Significant issues found - internal damage, major leaks Walk away (pre-purchase) or replace (failure inspection) Example Report Extract Compression Test Results: Cylinder 1 178 psi ✅ Pass - within specification Cylinder 2 175 psi ✅ Pass - within specification Cylinder 3 172 psi ✅ Pass - within specification Cylinder 4 80 psi ❌ Fail - significantly below specification Borescope Findings: Cylinder 4 shows scoring on the cylinder wall - likely caused by piston ring failure or foreign debris. Recommendation: Replacement is recommended. The engine has internal damage that cannot be repaired economically. Specialist Insights Real-World Anecdotal Validation The following insights are drawn from interviews with UK engine specialists who regularly perform engine inspections [EM-INTERVIEW]. "A customer was about to buy a used BMW 3 Series for £8,000. We did a full inspection - compression test, borescope, oil analysis. The borescope showed scoring on cylinder 3 - the engine was already failing. They walked away from the deal. The £200 inspection saved them £4,500 in engine replacement." - UK Engine Specialist Interview #34 [EM-INTERVIEW] (full names withheld at specialist's request) "Diagnostics can't see scoring on cylinder walls. It can't see worn piston rings. It can't see head gasket damage without a compression test. The physical inspection tells you things the computer doesn't know." - UK Engine Specialist Interview #35 [EM-INTERVIEW] "When you're buying a classic car, the engine is a big part of the value. A £300 inspection can reveal whether the engine is original, whether it's been rebuilt, and whether it's healthy. For a £20,000 classic, that's a small price to pay." - UK Engine Specialist Interview #36 [EM-INTERVIEW] How it works How Engines Market Works Four simple steps to get your engine inspection. 1 Submit Your Enquiry Enter your vehicle details. Tell us whether you need a pre-purchase inspection or a failure inspection. 2 Receive Quotes Within 30-60 minutes, you'll receive 3-5 quotes from vetted specialists offering inspection services. 3 Book Your Inspection Choose a specialist based on price, location, and reviews. Book a convenient time. 4 Get Your Report Attend the workshop for the inspection. Receive a written report with findings, photos, and recommendations. Get inspection quotes → Get a quote Frequently Asked Questions Common questions about engine inspection How much does an engine inspection cost? − Basic inspection £100-£150, full inspection £150-£250, comprehensive inspection £200-£300, classic/specialist £250-£400. Prices vary by vehicle type and region. What's the difference between diagnostics and inspection? + Diagnostics reads trouble codes from the ECU - finds electrical and sensor faults. Inspection is a physical examination - compression test, borescope, oil analysis. They're complementary services. When should I get an engine inspection? + Before buying a used car, after an unexplained failure, before a major trip, or when buying a classic car. If you're uncertain about the engine's condition, an inspection is the best investment. What does the inspection report include? + Visual inspection results, compression test figures, leak-down test results, borescope images (if performed), oil analysis results (if selected), condition assessment (pass/advisory/fail), and recommendations. Can I use the inspection for a private car sale? + Yes - a pre-purchase inspection is ideal for private sales. The buyer can see the condition of the engine before committing. It's also useful for the seller to demonstrate the vehicle's condition. Do I need to bring the car to the workshop? + Yes - the inspection requires physical access to the vehicle. The specialist will need to run the engine, perform compression tests, and use borescopes and other equipment. What if the inspection finds a problem? + If the problem is repairable, get repair quotes. If replacement is needed, get replacement quotes. If you're buying the car, the inspection gives you leverage to negotiate the price or walk away. Can I do an engine inspection myself? + You can do a basic visual inspection yourself. But compression tests, leak-down tests, and borescope inspections require specialist tools and expertise. A professional inspection is more thorough and provides a written report. faqs.question: Can I do an engine inspection myself? +
faqs.answer: You can do a basic visual inspection yourself. But compression tests, leak-down tests, and borescope inspections require specialist tools and expertise. A professional inspection is more thorough and provides a written report.

mainEntity.name: How much does an engine inspection cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Basic inspection £100-£150, full inspection £150-£250, comprehensive inspection £200-£300, classic/specialist £250-£400. Prices vary by vehicle type and region.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between diagnostics and inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diagnostics reads trouble codes from the ECU - finds electrical and sensor faults. Inspection is a physical examination - compression test, borescope, oil analysis. They're complementary services.

mainEntity.name: When should I get an engine inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before buying a used car, after an unexplained failure, before a major trip, or when buying a classic car. If you're uncertain about the engine's condition, an inspection is the best investment.

mainEntity.name: What does the inspection report include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visual inspection results, compression test figures, leak-down test results, borescope images (if performed), oil analysis results (if selected), condition assessment, and recommendations.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the inspection for a private car sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - a pre-purchase inspection is ideal for private sales. The buyer can see the condition of the engine before committing.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to bring the car to the workshop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the inspection requires physical access to the vehicle. The specialist will need to run the engine, perform compression tests, and use borescopes.
